notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. 65-year-old male admitted for upper GI bleed. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.66, creatinine 0.81-0.82, hemoglobin 12.7-14.1, platelets 233-235, sodium 139-140, wbc 7.2-7.8; vitals dbp 71-76, heart_rate 86-89, map 92-97, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-16, sbp 132-138, spo2 95-96, temp 36.6-36.8
Day 0 orders/meds/results: EGD: bleeding duodenal ulcer, treated with endoscopic clips; Pantoprazole 80 mg IV
Assessment and plan: Upper GI bleed. Hypertension. Acute blood loss anemia.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient seen and examined at bedside. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 0.79-0.84, hemoglobin 11.4-12.2, platelets 230-238, sodium 139-140, wbc 7.2-7.5; vitals dbp 71-76, heart_rate 85-87, map 92-96, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-16, sbp 132-137, spo2 95-97, temp 36.6-36.9
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Transfuse 1 unit packed red blood cells
Assessment and plan: Upper GI bleed. Hypertension. Acute blood loss anemia. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 65-year-old male, length of stay 4 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Upper GI bleed. Hypertension. Acute blood loss anemia. Follow up with primary care in one week. Patient seen and examined at bedside.
